title: Descent of ordinary blowup chart comparisons along an etale cover
statement: Let $X$ and $Z$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], $q:Z\to X$ a morphism, and $J\subset\mathcal O_X$ a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal [pqf-def-coherent]. Put $p:B=\operatorname{Bl}_JX\to X$ [def-nagata-global-blowup]. Let $(g_i:X_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i\to X)_{i\in I}$ be a jointly surjective family of etale morphisms [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Write $J_i=J\mathcal O_{X_i}$ and $Z_i=Z\times_X X_i$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal, def-pc-fibre-product]. Assume $J_i$ is generated by a finite nonempty set $E_i\subset A_i$ of non-zero-divisors (multiplication by each $a\in E_i$ is injective). Suppose that isomorphisms $\theta_i:Z_i\simeq\operatorname{Bl}_{J_i}X_i$ over $X_i$ are given, with no compatibility assumption on the $\theta_i$. Then on each affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}A_i[J_i/a]$ [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring] the extended ideal is generated by the non-zero-divisor $a$. For every flat $T\to Z_i$ [def-weil-flat-morphism], $J\mathcal O_T$ is invertible, meaning locally free of rank one as an ideal of $\mathcal O_T$. Compose $\theta_i$ with the canonical flat-base-change isomorphism $\operatorname{Bl}_{J_i}X_i\simeq B\times_X X_i$ [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map] and projection to $B$ to obtain $\varphi_i:Z_i\to B$. The $\varphi_i$ agree on $Z\times_X X_i\times_X X_j$. There is a unique $X$-isomorphism $\varphi:Z\simeq B$ restricting to these maps; its base change to $X_i$ is the composite just specified.

source.place: Expose VIII, proof of 3.4.6, printed p. 111, 'All claims can be checked etale locally'; expanded by Stacks 0805 (divisors.tex, lemma-flat-base-change-blowing-up), 0806 (divisors.tex, lemma-universal-property-blowing-up), 022C (topologies.tex), 023Q (descent.tex, lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms).

proof.text: Fix $i$ and $a\in E_i$. On $C=A_i[J_i/a]$, the extended ideal is $J_iC$ by [lemma-nagata-extended-ideal-affine-chart], equals $(a)$ by [lemma-nagata-chart-extended-ideal-principal], and multiplication by $a$ is injective by [lemma-nagata-chart-generator-regular]. Thus $C\to(a)$, $c\mapsto ac$, is a module isomorphism. The charts for $a\in E_i$ cover by [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-cover]. Pulling these opens across $\theta_i$ proves that $J\mathcal O_{Z_i}$ is locally a principal ideal generated by a non-zero-divisor.

Let $h:T\to Z_i$ be flat. On the inverse image of one of the preceding charts, let $a_T$ be the pulled-back generator. At $t\in T$, write $R=\mathcal O_{Z_i,h(t)}$ and $S=\mathcal O_{T,t}$. Multiplication by $a$ remains injective in $R$: in a localization, $a(c/s)=0$ implies $uac=0$ for some denominator $u$, hence $uc=0$. By [def-weil-flat-morphism], $S$ is a flat $R$-module. Tensor the injective map $R\xrightarrow{a}R$ with $S$; [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] makes the resulting multiplication by $a_T$ on $S$ injective. By [lemma-nagata-flat-pullback-ideal-pow] with $n=1$, the extended ideal is the image of the pulled-back ideal; [def-pc-module-pullback] identifies its map locally with $\mathcal O_T\xrightarrow{a_T}\mathcal O_T$. Thus this image is $(a_T)$ and is isomorphic to $\mathcal O_T$. Successive extension is extension along the composite: the two inverse-image closed subschemes are canonically equal by the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product], so their defining kernels [def-nagata-extended-ideal] agree. Hence this ideal is precisely $J\mathcal O_T$. The inverse-image opens cover $T$, proving invertibility.

source.place: Tag 0805, lemma-flat-base-change-blowing-up, proof: injectivity of flat pullback of ideal inclusions

proof.text: Regard $\{X_i\to X\}$ as a covering of the object $X\to X$ in the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. It is an fpqc covering by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-finer-than-etale]. Its pullbacks to any $X$-scheme are fpqc coverings by [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change]. In particular this gives covers of $Z$, $B$, $Z_i$, and their iterated overlaps. Every map in such a covering is flat by [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]; thus $Z_{ij}=Z\times_XX_i\times_XX_j\to Z_i$ is flat. Step 2 applies to $Z_{ij}$, so $J\mathcal O_{Z_{ij}}$ is invertible.

Etale maps are flat by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. By [thm-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change], the specified comparison yields an isomorphism $\alpha_i:Z_i\xrightarrow{\theta_i}\operatorname{Bl}_{J_i}X_i\xrightarrow{\operatorname{bc}_{g_i}}B_i=B\times_XX_i$, with the two factors exchanged from the convention of [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map]. Set $\varphi_i=\operatorname{pr}_B\alpha_i$. On $Z_{ij}$ both $\varphi_i\operatorname{pr}_i$ and $\varphi_j\operatorname{pr}_j$ are $X$-morphisms to $B$. By Step 3 their common source has invertible extended ideal. The uniqueness assertion of [thm-nagata-blowup-universal-property] makes the two maps equal. More explicitly, in its invertible-quotient formulation the quotient is necessarily the canonical surjection onto $J\mathcal O_{Z_{ij}}$: composing it with the specified ideal inclusion is the fixed map from $J$ to $\mathcal O_{Z_{ij}}$, and the inclusion is injective. Thus the maps induce the same quotient. This checks compatibility without a compatibility assumption on the $\theta_i$.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] to the fpqc cover $\{Z_i\to Z\}$ from Step 3 and the compatible $\varphi_i$ of Step 4. It gives a unique morphism $\varphi:Z\to B$ with these restrictions. The maps $p\varphi$ and $q$ have equal restrictions $Z_i\to X$, so the uniqueness part of the same descent statement, now with target $X$, gives $p\varphi=q$. Pairing with the projection to $X_i$, the base change $\varphi_{X_i}:Z_i\to B_i$ is $\alpha_i$: both maps have components $\varphi_i$ and the structure map to $X_i$, and [def-pc-fibre-product] determines a map from its two components.

Write $\beta_i=\alpha_i^{-1}:B_i\to Z_i$ and $\psi_i=\operatorname{pr}_Z\beta_i:B_i\to Z$. For $B_{ij}=B\times_XX_i\times_XX_j$, pull back $\alpha_i$ and $\alpha_j$ to obtain $Z_{ij}\to B_{ij}$. Their $B$-components agree by Step 4, and their components to $X_i$ and $X_j$ are the same structure maps. By [def-pc-fibre-product] the two isomorphisms are equal, so their inverses are equal. Composing these inverses with $Z_{ij}\to Z$ proves $\psi_i\operatorname{pr}_i=\psi_j\operatorname{pr}_j$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] for the fpqc cover $\{B_i\to B\}$ of Step 3 there is a unique $\psi:B\to Z$ with restrictions $\psi_i$. Equality over $X$ follows by the same uniqueness argument with target $X$.

On $Z_i$, the equality $\psi\varphi=\mathrm{id}_Z$ reduces to $\beta_i\alpha_i=\mathrm{id}_{Z_i}$ followed by $Z_i\to Z$. On $B_i$, the equality $\varphi\psi=\mathrm{id}_B$ reduces to $\alpha_i\beta_i=\mathrm{id}_{B_i}$ followed by $B_i\to B$. The uniqueness part of [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] on the two fpqc covers proves both global identities. Thus $\varphi$ is the required $X$-isomorphism. Any other such isomorphism has the same restrictions to $Z_i$ and equals $\varphi$ by that same uniqueness assertion. Its base changes are precisely the $\alpha_i$ already checked in Step 5.
